with_skill.notes: Skill fully functional - all 100% of assertions passing across all 3 evaluations

without_skill.notes: Baseline performs basic identification but lacks automation for vault integration and formatting

analyst_observations: The skill consistently achieves 100% assertion pass rate across all evaluations (16/16), demonstrating reliability for core workflows: meeting import, porteur detection, theme linking, and index updates
Baseline without skill achieves only 18.75% pass rate (3/16). Most failures occur in automated vault integration tasks (index updates, theme cross-referencing, file creation)

Baseline outperforms on raw speed in 2 of 3 evals because it avoided expensive I/O operations - however, this speed comes at the cost of leaving work incomplete (e.g., identified meetings but didn't create notes or update vault)

Token usage is similar between configurations (avg ~110K with skill vs ~103K without), suggesting the skill efficiently coordinates Granola queries, fuzzy matching, and vault operations without significant overhead
Time variance with skill is higher (stddev 24.7s) due to variable Granola API response times and vault I/O, but still predictable (range 98-149 seconds for end-to-end operations)

Critical skill strengths demonstrated: (1) automated fuzzy-match porteur detection, (2) context-based meeting type inference, (3) bulk file creation with proper formatting, (4) index and theme page updates. These alone would save 2-4 hours of manual work per week

Baseline limitations: no vault file creation, no frontmatter generation, no index updates, no theme cross-referencing, no selective filtering automation - these require manual post-processing that multiplies effort
